decisions.reason: As a straightforward extension of the bakery’s core rye range, it likely meets at least minimum aspiration levels and is cheap to carry with existing skills and production.
Because it is both close to the established seasonal offer and explicitly presented as a flagship, management would be inclined to retain it unless results clearly fell far below aspirations.

This seeded rye mixed bread fits current customer tastes while relying on familiar recipes, ingredients, and processes, so boundedly rational management would usually continue it absent strong negative signals.
Its darker barley-malt rye profile is somewhat more niche than the standard breads, but it still uses the firm’s core bread-making capabilities and can be tolerated while demand becomes clearer.

Marzipan stollen is a plausible seasonal variant within the firm’s confectionery competence, though as a non-flagship holiday line it faces a somewhat higher risk of being cut if first-season sales disappointed.

The ancient grain bread is the most novel and potentially less predictable of the bread launches, but its artisanal fit and use of the firm’s existing baking resources make continued trial more likely than immediate withdrawal.
